# Sea Raider Templates

*Pages PDF 4-7*

## Old Weirde’s Incunabulum
sorcery. These edifices spill forth dark ships and sea monsters, who despoil and destroy all they meet. Of the denizens of these fleets, we know little — and I have found the Elves reluctant to speak freely on these matters. 

On occasion, I venture a little further from my hearth to enjoy a libation at the Frisky Seagoat, an inn by the naval docks in Flottenliegeplatz. What the patrons lack in decorum and intact limbs, they more than make up with tattoos depicting sea serpents and great krakens, and tall tales from the sea. 

Nevertheless, I have gathered fragments of information from Abbot Bruggeman of Manannsheim, my dear friend Professor Kikkert of Baron Henryk’s College in Marienburg, and Grandmaster Hrofil Halfdan of the Sons of Manann. Consistent accounts from the northern coasts speak of black-clad reavers dressed in reptilian cloaks, who descend on isolated coastal settlements to murder and enslave the residents. By the time local rulers muster a response, the Dark Elves are long gone — one notorious example is the ill-fated village of Debnietz, where the inhabitants were flayed and nailed to the cliffs. 

During a recent visit, I heard a yarn from a one-armed Nordlander, a gentleman of morose disposition and powerful odor. As the rain lashed on the panes, he told of a galley in full sail that blew into the Kriedeklippe Bight, two days before Mitterfruhl. She was listing badly and no crewman answered the warning cries to stay away from the rocks. When the inevitable happened and she crashed onto a reef, the salvage crew found a harrowing mystery. Bloodstains spattered the deck and other than the captain, no soul was on board. The poor wretch clung to life, pinned to the mast with barbed quarrels, his flesh horribly lacerated and his mind completely gone. 

When researching any matter related to the Elves, I find Algnar’s A Man Amongst the Elves informative. He mentions an ancient schism between the Elven folk, when those from the northern reaches of their fabled isle embraced the dark powers and rebelled against the rightful king. They were banished, or retreated, to the icy lands north of Lustria. There is little more in the Human writings I have to hand… as ever, I come up against the limits of prior scholarship. I determined to ask an Asur acquaintance for further enlightenment. 

The first mate of a Wasteland merchantman sucked on his pipe and nodded through the smoke. He had seen similar and worse. It was the Elf folk — not the haughty Elves we know in Altdorf and Marienburg, nor their cousins the ‘Wood Elves’ who dwell in the Laurelorn and Athel Loren. The Wastelander whispered of their vicious kin, the ‘Dark Elves’, who raid our coasts and attack ships from their sleek black vessels. 

One foggy evening in Erntezeit, I set out to consult with Loremaster Illissia Waysworn of the Sapherian Embassy over a delicious repast in the New World Dinery. 

My attempts to research these corsairs have proved challenging. Historical accounts recount them coming to the Old World from hulking fortresses, which float on the waves through powerful 

It was not an illuminating conversation. While the Loremaster resembles a woman half my age, she speaks with more condescension than the memories of my grandfather from youth. 

Illissia proceeded to give a detailed explanation of a ‘schism’, taking to use salt and pepper as visual aids, lest my apparently frail Human mind became lost upon this compelling journey of revelation. I nearly complained to her that I was well equipped, being one of Altdorf’s top scholars, to understand the basis of Elven history and culture, but thought better of it. The grasp of knowledge and haughty superiority born of immortality she commands mean that any disagreement with her runs the risk of thorough intellectual humiliation. 

She continued in this fashion, eager that I understand Ulthuan vociferously opposes the Dark Elves. Illisia sensed my frustration but did not allay it. She gave a wry smile and explained with a gratingly clear and careful manner that both groups of Elves, those who inhabit the island continent of Ulthuan and those they call the Druchii, stemmed from the same source but now contrasted greatly. I tried to understand the nuances behind these differences, but despite being told of the diverse degrees to which various principles are embodied in a multitude of gods, and which strategies and armaments are preferred by divergent military traditions, the only distinction that made real sense to me was that of their attire. 

I returned home in a sour mood, alleviated only by Frau Weirde’s welcome embrace. Yet it seems Ranald was smiling on me that night, as I received a missive from Kaia, an Elven travelling companion far more forthcoming than her Sapherian cousin. We met several days later in a small lodging house on the Bruckthin road, as Kaia prefers to stay away from the city. After talking briefly of mutual acquaintances and the rose-tinted past, I asked her about the Dark Elves. She paused for a moment, then told me what she knew of their culture and origins. 

‘The Druchii are not a secret. We don’t hide the shame of our brethren. Yet we do not feel it necessary to explain our affairs to Humans, as you could not hope to understand. These are not simply mutants or like those Men who turn to the great enemy. Perhaps it is easiest to consider the ‘Dark Elves’ as a dark, wild, and unrestrained side of our people — they are what happens should we fall out of balance and submit to our worst nature.’ 

Thousands of years ago, an Elven prince was denied the Phoenix Throne. He and his followers accepted this decision at first, but they harboured resentment and, many centuries later, tried to seize the crown by force. Our creator, Asuryan, intervened to frustrate his ambition, and so this prince rebelled and turned to the worship of gods feared or mistrusted by most Elves. This prince studied forbidden rites and grew to become a great sorcerer; we know him as the Witch King now. He and his followers instigated a civil war we remember as the Kinstrife. 

The Witch King was eventually defeated, so took his people to Naggaroth where they dwell to this day, growing ever more bitter.’ 

‘They prey on lesser species and Elf alike. The Black Arks were torn from the land of Ulthuan itself, now they sail the world to despoil for the Witch King. He rules from the frozen land of Naggaroth, far to the west. His subjects prize murder and compete with cruelty to achieve power over one another. Their survival in their bleak land requires captive labour and endless sacrifices to the gods, so raiders set out across the Great Ocean to take Humans back to their cursed land. As I said, they are the worst we could become…’ 

I remarked that Kaia was one of the Eonir, and she had told me in the past she has no love for Ulthuan. She conceded the point, and let me know the arrogance of the Asur towards her people is antagonising, yet the depredations of the Druchii are far worse. 

‘The raids on your coastline originate from the Black Arks, where a fleetmaster lords over many smaller tributary vessels. Some Druchii ships are grim reflections of the High Elf ships, swift under sail and crewed by especially adept sailors. Others are nightmarish seaborne chariots, pulled through the waves by Sea Dragons and beasts from the depths. These are commanded by those Druchii beastmasters who subjugate wild creatures of land and sea. Others harness the worst magicks, hoping to tame the darkest forces in service of their ambitions and their race’s conquests.’ 

Kaia fell quiet, reflecting to herself on these grave matters. I ventured a question. ‘What do these Druchii want?’ 

‘Do you recall that day you took me to visit the Imperial Zoo?’ Kaia wrinkled her nose; she hadn’t enjoyed the experience. ‘We witnessed a juvenile Mournfang being fed a live goat and watched as it toyed with its prey. Such creatures need to eat, yet they take pleasure in the hunt and the suffering they cause before the kill. The Druchii want to slaughter and enslave the Elves and Humanity alike… but not before they enjoy our agonies. Be thankful they fight amongst themselves, for if they truly unite, it will bring doom to the lands of Men and Elves.’ 

I thanked Kaia for her candour and asked how she knew so much about these matters. 

‘I cannot say.’ Her eyes flicked briefly to a scar on her left hand which I had not seen before. Perhaps a rune, although defaced with more scar tissue… Kaia was not forthcoming and I thought it prudent not to pursue the matter. 

I have determined to avoid the coastline after dark in future. 

## **Sea Raider Templates**
The following templates will help GMs create Dark Elf reavers for their games, or modify the profile of Humans and other creatures to reflect other seaborne raiders. This could include Norse reavers, Human corsairs, Goblins, or Undead pirates — with a little work, the GM can create a motley bunch of seaborne cut-throats. 

## **Dark Elves**
Over 5,000 years ago, civil war tore apart the Elven species, an event known as the Sundering. In defeat, the Dark Elves retreated to the cold land of Naggaroth, embittered and corrupt. Today, the Druchii’s hatred drives them to unfathomable cruelties, consumed by their loathing for their High Elf kin and all other species. 

**DARK ELF**

| M | WS | BS | S | T | I | Ag | Dex | Int | WP | Fel | W |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|5|40|40|30|30|50|40|40|40|40|30|13|

**Traits:** Hatred (High Elves), Night Vision, Weapon +7 **Optional:** Armour 3, Frenzy, Ranged +9 (60), Spellcaster (Any), Stealthy 

## **Reaver Captain**
The captains of raiding ships are accomplished warriors in their own right. They dominate their crew through fear and the promise of plunder and glory. Whether on land or at sea, a reaver captain must prove their prowess or risk mutiny from their dangerous crew. 

**REAVER CAPTAIN**

| M | WS | BS | S | T | I | Ag | Dex | Int | WP | Fel | W |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
||+20|+20|+10|+10|+20|+20|+10|+10|+20|+20||

**Skills:** Athletics +15, Climb +5, Cool +15, Dodge +10, Endurance +10, Intimidate +15, Intuition +15, Language (Any) +20, Leadership +15, Melee (Any two) +15, Navigation +10, Perception +15, Ranged (Any) +15, Row +10, Sail +15, Swim +10 

**Talents:** Catfall, Combat Reflexes, Dual Wielder, Furious Assault, In-fighter, Inspiring, Menacing, Pilot, Public Speaking, Read/Write, Sea Legs, Strong Swimmer 

**Trappings:** 2 Hand Weapons, Leather or Mail Armour, Weapon (Any Ranged) 

## Sea Dragon Cloaks
Dark Elf corsairs wear cloaks fashioned from the hide of a sea dragon. These mark their status and offer protection from the elements and from hostile attacks. You can equip Druchii Reaver Captains, Chief Mates, and Corsairs with a Sea Dragon Cloak — providing an additional 2 AP to the Body Hit Location, with the Partial Flaw. Wearers must treat their cloak regularly with a special slime of reptilian origin — if not slathered, it begins to disintegrate, a process that takes one week. A fresh application of slime restores the cloak to normal. 

## **Chief Mate**
Every Reaver Captain relies on a trusted lackey to back up their commands and knock heads if there are signs of mutiny. The title varies — whether it’s a Chief Mate, First Officer, Bosun, or Scurvy Henchman, they all serve to enforce the captain’s authority and do the jobs they delegate. 

**CHIEF MATE**

||+15|+10|+10|+10|+15|+15|+10|+5|+10|+15||

**Skills:** Athletics +10, Climb +5, Cool +10, Dodge +5, Endurance +10, Intimidate +10, Intuition +10, Language (Any) +20, Leadership +5, Melee (Any two) +10, Navigation +10, Perception +10, Ranged (Any) +10, Row +10, Sail +15, Swim +10

## **Corsair**
A corsair combines prowess as a sailor with a fighter’s skill and courage. They lead boarding actions and fight in raiding parties on shore. Dark Elf corsairs are notorious for their cruelty. Human corsairs come from all maritime cultures, from the Old World, Araby, Sartosa, or further afield, often armed with weapons characteristic of their native land. On ships, they man the cannon or bolt throwers during a sea battle. 

**CORSAIR**

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
||+10|+5|+5|+5|+10|+5|+5||+5|+5||

**Skills:** Athletics +5, Climb +5, Cool +10, Dodge +10, Melee (Basic) +10, Navigation +5, Ranged (Any) +10, Row +5, Sail +5, Swim +5 

**Talents:** Dual Wielder, In-fighter, Sea Legs

**Trappings:** 2 Hand Weapons, Leather or Mail Armour, Weapon (Any Ranged)

## **’ Ship S Crew**
These are disreputable sailors who lack the combat skills of the corsairs, although they can handle themselves in a boarding action. These sailors are treacherous swabs and scurvy ne’er-dowells, who resent their measly share of the plunder and remain loyal mainly through fear of the captain and the corsairs.

## **Oarsman**
Oared galleys and longships are common amongst reavers. Reaver captains usually force their thralls or captives to row, chained to benches, spurred on by the relentless beat of a drum and fear of the lash. . 

**OARSMAN**

| M | WS | BS | S | T | I | Ag | Dex | Int | WP | Fel | W |

||||+10|+5||||||+5||

**Skills:** Cool +5, Dodge +5, Endurance +15, Row +20

**Talents:** Old Salt, Sea Legs, Stone Soup, Strong Back

**Trappings:** Chains, Ragged Garments

## **Lookout**
Eagle-eyed crewmen act as lookouts, scouring the sea for prey from the crow’s nest or forging ahead as scouts onshore. They are nimble and observant, adept at avoiding fights with their fellow reavers. Dark Elf lookouts range ahead of raiding parties to uncover possible resistance. Amongst Human reavers, lookouts are typically the youngest amongst the crew.and fear of the lash. . 

## **Lookout**
## **Beastmaster**
Raiding parties may include animal handlers, who goad their beasts to hunt and drag down victims on the shore. Dark Elf beastmasters are renowned for the monstrous beasts they control, such as Hydras or Karybdis. Lowlier Druchii train packs of warhounds and take depraved pleasure from setting them on captives. Norse beastmasters breed slavering wolves, hungry for flesh, and there are tales of Arabyan pirates training vicious apes to fight on their behalf. 

**BEASTMASTER M WS BS S T I Ag Dex Int WP Fel W** +5 +10 +5 +5 +5 +5 

**Skills:** Animal Care +10, Animal Training +15, Charm Animal +15, Cool +5, Drive +10, Intimidate +5, Melee (Basic) +10, Ranged (Entangling) +10, Ride +15, Track +10 

**Talents:** Animal Affinity, Crack the Whip, Read/Write

**Trappings:** Crop or Whip, Net

## **Druchii Sorceress**
The sisters of the Dark Covenant are sorceresses who wield some of the most powerful magic in the world. They are influential within Dark Elf society — should they choose to travel abroad with corsairs to further their ambitions, few dare refuse them passage.
